records.name: Hawaii
records.current_summary: A July 2026 national legal-risk map lists Hawaii among the federation's Most Protective states — those that have "gone above and beyond" in safeguarding transgender people's rights — and equality-map research counts Hawaii among the states whose healthcare "shield" laws protect trans people, their families and providers, including visitors travelling from states where care is banned, against out-of-state legal action.  Federal 2025 document and passport restrictions still apply here as in every state.

sources.claim: July 2026 national legal-risk ranking built from a rubric over thousands of tracked anti-trans bills (youth-care bans, bathroom bans, birth-certificate/driver-license restrictions, end of legal recognition): Hawaii sits in the fifteen-state 'Most Protective' tier (CA, CO, CT, HI, IL, MA, MD, MN, NJ, NM, NY, OR, RI, VT, WA), whose laws have 'gone above and beyond in safeguarding' trans rights. Contrast tier: worst-law states carry up to 5-year prison terms (Idaho) or arrest policy for gender-identity bathroom use (Florida).

MAP Transgender Healthcare Equality Map (data as of 27 Sep 2026) lists Hawaii as 'State has shield law or executive order 2026': the shield/refuge law protects patients and providers from civil or criminal charges when care legal here was banned in the home state — directly relevant to visitors travelling from ban states. National picture on the page: 16 states + D.C. (38% of trans population 13+) hold shields; 32 states + 5 territories (56%) hold none; youth-care bans tracked, some permanently blocked.

records.name: Centro
records.current_summary: The region contains two of the six regions with the highest recorded counts of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence in the 2012-2025 region-by-region study maintained by the country's principal LGBT monitoring project.  Against that stands the strongest judicial response to transphobic violence recorded anywhere in the country: in January 2025 a first-instance court in this region's main university city recognised a "transphobic motive" in the punitive rape of a trans sex worker, sentenced the perpetrator, awarded damages to the victim and to the association that supports trans sex workers, and - for the first time - admitted the national trans-movement organisation as civil party.  For a visitor the combination is specific: the highest-frequency regions of the country's violence record are here, but so is a documented court that named transphobic motive and ordered reparation.

sources.claim: Dire news-agency report (24 Jan 2025): a Bologna first-instance court recognised a "transphobic motive" in the punitive rape of a trans sex worker, sentenced the perpetrator, awarded damages to the victim and to the trans-movement association that helps sex workers, and for the first time admitted the Movimento Identita Trans (MIT) as civil party - the strongest judicial recognition of transphobic aggravation recorded in this country.

Progetto Gionata region-by-region study of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence 2012-2025: names the Italian regions with the highest victim counts, six of them ranking at the top; Lazio and Toscana (both inside Centro) are two of the six highest-victim regions, alongside Lombardia, Piemonte (Nord-Ovest), Campania and Puglia (Sud). Provides the per-region violence distribution used to score all Italian units.

On August 30, 2025 Rome's municipal administration announced that the Consiglio di Stato (the country's highest administrative court, seated in Rome) had upheld the city's 2022 removal of Pro Vita & Famiglia posters attacking 'gender' ideology in schools, on the ground that the images — one showing a boy being given a red hairbow — were discriminatory and that public spaces may not be used for messages that 'generate alarmism, fear or serious disturbance', particularly concerning minors. The anti-trans campaign behind the posters had collected 105,000 online signatures. The ruling is a dated judicial outcome in the region's largest city confirming that anti-trans public messaging can be restricted there, an institutional datapoint for this region record, which otherwise centres on violence statistics and the transphobic-motive verdict in Perugia.

On March 5, 2026 the Court of Cassation confirmed the appeal-court acquittal of trans woman Pinheiro Reis Duarte Hudson ('Patrizia') over the April 27, 2021 death of Samuele De Paoli in Perugia, finding the death was caused by cardiac arrhythmia from accidental compression during a scuffle that De Paoli started, making the acquittal on the charge of homicide final. The case, in this region's main university city, was a national anti-trans media flashpoint, and the definitive judicial outcome favoured the trans defendant. For this record it documents that the region's courts and the highest ordinary court decided a high-profile trans-related case on the facts, complementing the record's claim about judicial responses to transphobic violence.

records.name: Nord-Ovest
records.current_summary: This region hosts the country's first and second practical civic gender-recognition schemes: Milano's "registro di genere" - chosen name on civic and municipal documents, public-transport subscriptions and staff badges, created by a 2022 council motion brought by the country's first elected transgender councillor - and Torino's analogous "Identita Alias" practice at the municipality and the public libraries. For a gender-nonconforming visitor these determine whether a ticket window or municipal desk becomes an argument.  Against this, the 2012-2025 region-by-region study of anti-LGBT hate-motivated violence names this region's two leading regions among the country's six highest-victim regions.

sources.claim: LifeGate: Milan inaugurated Italy's first gender registry ('registro di genere'), letting transgender people use their chosen name on civic and municipal documents — presented as a milestone for transgender rights in the country; the record ties it to a 2022 council motion by the country's first elected transgender councillor, with Turin's parallel 'Identita Alias' practice at municipality and libraries.

records.name: Nord-Est
records.current_summary: The region's dominant constituent authority carries a documented record of official acts of hostility toward trans people. In 2014, following a council deliberation, the regional government formally instituted a mandatory "Natural Family Day" on the last school day before the Christmas holidays and rejected the aims and content of the WHO Regional Office's Standards for Sexuality Education in Europe, committing to deploy every available instrument against their adoption in the region's schools (official regional bulletin, December 2014).  In July 2018 the regional council approved a further motion pledging support for "those who fight in defence of the natural family" and for natalist policies, attacking the civil-unions law, and dismissing Pride marches as "carnival farces". These official acts create a clearly unwelcome climate signal; neither imposes a criminal sanction, fine or enforcement exposure on a visitor.

records.name: Sud

In October 2025 at a commuter railway station in the region's main metropolitan area an activist - president of a local LGBT association - was subjected to an escalating verbal homophobic attack ending in threats of stabbing by two young men. records.name: Isole
records.current_summary: At roughly 5 a.m. on 26 April 2025 three young men were beaten in a fast-food restaurant in this region's largest city solely because they were gay; the victims were hospitalised, video of the attack later circulated publicly, and the prosecutor's office reconstructed the sequence - insults and threats first, then the physical assault.  A June 2026 press survey of reporting from the island documents a sustained pattern rather than isolated events: rising homophobic bullying, violence against LGBTIA+ people and associated suicides, with multiple cases listed. The pattern is qualitative but official: a hospitalisation-level public assault and an prosecutorial reconstruction sit alongside a growing documented toll.

records.name: Alberta
records.current_summary: In December 2024 this province enacted a package of three laws affecting transgender people as a class: school rules requiring parental notification and consent before staff use a student's gender-related chosen name or pronouns; a prohibition on puberty blockers and hormone therapy for minors; and related vital-statistics amendments. Trans and intersex advocacy organisations said at the time they would continue legal action.  In December 2025 the government invoked the constitutional override clause to shield all three laws from judicial remedy. Two national 2SLGBTQ+ organisations, together with five gender-diverse young people, say the constitutional challenge continues despite the shield - a provincial posture of legislating trans-targeting rules and then placing them beyond the courts.

sources.claim: CBC (4 Dec 2024): Alberta's trio of trans-youth bills passed final legislative stage — the Education Amendment Act 2024 (parental opt-in for classroom instruction, student pronoun and sport rules), a health-statutes act barring certain gender-affirming care for minors, plus sports policy. Egale Canada and the Skipping Stone Foundation announced constitutional litigation, calling the package discriminatory.

CBC (Dec 2024): Bill 9, the Protecting Alberta's Children Statutes Amendment Act, passed at the tail of the fall sitting, invoking the Charter's notwithstanding clause to shield the three trans-youth laws from legal challenge for years; Egale Canada, Skipping Stone Foundation and five families said their court challenge to Bill 26 continues regardless. Result: laws in force, constitutional litigation pending.
